main_update_risks: FHIR-origin STU3 element properties in FASTO use path-specific IRIs such as Resource.element; the supplied FHIR R5 TTL uses generic property IRIs with path-specific annotations, so most object properties require replacement or review.

FASTO-created classes, properties, and individuals were minted inside FHIR namespaces; several collide with or resemble R5 canonical classes/properties and should be moved to a FASTO namespace or explicitly profiled.

Choice elements and renamed clinical-context fields, including onset[x], value[x], context/encounter, assertedDate/recordedDate, and ProcedureRequest/ServiceRequest, require manual migration checks before updating OWL axioms.

FASTO domain/range/subPropertyOf axioms attached to FHIR-origin IRIs are likely local profiling constraints, not reusable FHIR R5 axioms; they should be represented in a profile layer rather than as modifications of FHIR IRIs.
